meta.title: Fleetwright — Browser fleets that never collide
meta.description: One control plane for Playwright claim workers, crawlers and a local AI agent. Database-enforced single claims, crash-safe leases and latency you can audit stage by stage.

headline: Browser Fleets
That Never Collide
hero.subhead: Designed to coordinate 70+ Playwright workers, crawlers and a local AI agent from one control plane — with database-enforced single claims and latency you can audit stage by stage.
hero.statsCaption: Design targets. Measured results publish after the Phase 5 load test.

problem.text: Fifty workers watch the same board. A load appears. Twelve of them click Book in the same second. Without one source of truth, you just booked the same load twelve times — and the client finds out from the broker.

claimRace.title: Many vessels. Exactly one lands.
claimRace.fallbackNote: Interactive 3D view unavailable — the steps below describe the same sequence.

steps.title: A watcher sees the load
steps.body: Watchers read the board's JSON responses, not the DOM, and publish a DETECTED event with a seen_at timestamp.

steps.title: Every matching actor races
steps.body: Filters route the job to pre-warmed actors whose sessions are already logged in. Redis gives a fast first filter — never the final word.

steps.title: Postgres picks one winner
steps.body: INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on (tenant_id, target_job_key). The database's unique key decides. Everyone else gets nothing to act on.

steps.title: A fencing token guards the click
steps.body: The lease carries a monotonic token. A worker that paused past its lease is rejected by the database clock, not its own.

steps.title: Confirmed — or reconciled, never retried blind
steps.body: A crash mid-action becomes UNKNOWN. The reconciler checks the board's bookings before it confirms or releases the job.

workers.title: Built for the three jobs clients actually post.

cards.title: Claim worker
cards.body: Watchers, actors and a coordinator that scale from 50 to 70+ workers without duplicate bookings. Sessions stay warm; OTP refresh is automatic.
points: Crash recovery, verified by chaos tests (Phase 5)

cards.title: Crawler
cards.body: Crawl jobs defined as data, per-domain politeness, retries with jitter, and alarms that catch the silent layout change before the client does.
points: Proxy and captcha adapters per client
SSRF egress guard on every fetch (planned)

cards.title: Fleetwright Agent
cards.body: A lightweight local app that drives your own Chrome across tabs. It drafts, researches and fills — and asks before it publishes, sends or buys.
points: Page text treated as untrusted data

workers.note: What each worker type is designed to do. The panels are illustrative mock data; measured results publish after the Phase 5 load test.

latency.title: Six timestamps. No averaged-away excuses.
latency.note: Every claim is stamped at each stage. Reports split publish→detect from detect→action, with p50 / p95 / p99 per stage.

stages.label: Published
stages.body: Ground truth from the board's own event log.

stages.label: Queued
stages.body: Filters matched; the job enters the cell's stream.

stages.label: Leased
stages.body: Postgres grants the single lease and its fencing token.

stages.label: Act sent
stages.body: The warm page clicks, or the session's HTTP action fires.

stages.label: Confirmed
stages.body: The board confirms the booking; the audit log closes the loop.

cells.title: When one cell fails, the fleet keeps claiming.
cells.body: A cell is a Redis, its watchers and its worker pool. The coordinator routes each tenant to a cell, so adding capacity is a config change — and a failing cell takes nothing else down with it.
cells.liveRegionFailed: Cell A is offline. Its tenants are rerouted to cell B, which keeps claiming.
cells.liveRegionRestored: Cell A is restored and claiming again.

guardrails.title: Strict by default.

items.title: MFA for every operator
items.body: TOTP enforced; argon2id hashing; RBAC checked server-side on every endpoint.

items.title: Tenant isolation in the database
items.body: tenant_id on every row with Postgres Row-Level Security.

items.title: Append-only audit log
items.body: Every mutation and every claim action is recorded.

items.title: No third-party captcha defeat
items.body: Solver services are added per client, after legal review and written authorisation.

items.title: US + EU law register
items.body: CFAA, GDPR, AI Act Art. 50 and the CRA mapped to design rules — reviewed before any real target.

items.title: Secrets never logged
items.body: OTP codes and cookies are redacted by a logging filter, with tests that fail if one ever appears in a log.

guardrails.note: Design commitments from the build plan. Each ships with automated tests in its phase — none is claimed as done until those tests pass.

title: Walk The Fleet
Before It Exists
closing.body: The console prototype runs on mock data generated from the same contract the backend will implement.

footer.note: Fleetwright is a portfolio project. The demo target is a fictitious load board we built — nothing here points at a real third-party site.
